blocks.x: Honest quantum strategy: use cases triaged on verifiable criteria, a vendor-neutral posture, baselines measured before any hardware is booked — and a roadmap whose milestones are kill criteria, not keynote dates.
A quantum strategy is mostly a classical strategy with kill criteria

Most quantum strategy is either hype (quantum will solve everything by 2027) or dismissal (check back in 2035). Both waste money. The honest middle: triage your problem estate against criteria that can be verified — problem structure, data encoding cost, tolerance for noise, and whether a strong classical baseline even exists to beat.

The deliverable is a portfolio with three lists: problems worth formulating now, problems to watch as hardware improves, and problems where classical HPC is the right answer today — plus the PQC risk register, because the one quantum-adjacent deadline that is real is the cryptography one.
Below: the failure modes that capture strategies into vendor keynotes, the reference architecture of the triage process, and the console that tracks the roadmap honestly.
Four ways quantum strategies get captured by hype
Each failure mode spends real budget on unmeasurable outcomes — the countermeasures make every next step falsifiable and every claim reproducible.
